clusters.title: Commercial kitchen staff exposed to high levels of air pollution, study finds
clusters.neutral_headline: Commercial kitchen staff exposed to high levels of air pollution, study finds

items.title: Commercial kitchen staff exposed to high levels of air pollution, study finds
items.standfirst: US research says nitrogen dioxide in restaurants that cook with gas can exceed WHO limits, which also affects dinersEach time we enjoy a meal out or order a takeaway, someone cooks for us in a commercial kitchen. In the UK, 3.6 million people work in catering and hospitality. In the US it is estimated at close to 16 million. A first-of-its-kind study in the US has found catering staff can experience high air pollution at work – and that this can affect diners too.Dr Drew Michanowicz, senior author of the study at non-profit research institute PSE Healthy Energy, said: “I was motivated by what we have learned over the years about what just 30 minutes of gas cooking can do to air quality in homes with the realisation that millions of people cook for a living for hours on end.” Continue reading...

clusters.title: The Guardian view on food security: we have just-in-time, we need just-in-case | Editorial
clusters.neutral_headline: The Guardian view on food security: we have just-in-time,...

items.title: The Guardian view on food security: we have just-in-time, we need just-in-case | Editorial
items.standfirst: Experts are warning that the UK is unprepared for crises. A refrigerator cyber-attack scare in France is the latest reminder of the risksWhat’s worrying French supermarket bosses should be prompting British ministers to action. On Sunday, hackers forced up the temperatures of refrigerators in hundreds of food stores across France to as high as 50C, resulting in waste and fires. Beyond the immediate destruction and inconvenience, it raised the prospect of other malicious actors finding new ways to play havoc with the food chain.Only weeks before, 150 experts together warned the British government that it does not have a plan to feed people in a crisis ­– and that the west is entering an era in which not only disruption but the weaponisation of food is a real possibility. “The public has been led to assume that food will simply be there,” they wrote. “It may not be.”Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article?
